land.text: the whole Greek state, taken over by Karamanlis's civilian government on 24 July 1974

correction.text: the Greek state as the Third Hellenic Republic from the fall of the junta, unchanged in outline from the 1976 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page gives 'Established: 24 July 1974' while Cliopatria's first row begins in 1976 and its junta row runs on through 1975 (123,711 km2). The junta's 1973 shape and the 1976 shape differ by 1,694 km2 (about 1.4%), a rendering difference rather than a border change; no page opened records a Greek territorial change in 1974-76.
122,017 km2 against the infobox 131,957 km2 (no year given on the page): ratio 0.92, within a factor of two. Nothing on the page changes the land in 1976-91.

121,731 km2, 286 km2 (0.2%) less than 1976-91. The pages opened (this one and Metapolitefsi) are silent on any Greek border change in 1992 (it coincides only with the Cliopatria neighbour row changing from Yugoslavia to Macedonia, 1992), so the difference is read as a grid effect; unverified: page budget.
Same outline and area (121,731 km2) as 1992-2023.

ledger.note: 1974: the junta falls and the Third Hellenic Republic begins on 24 July. Infobox 'Established: 24 July 1974', 'the fall of the Greek military junta'; the Metapolitefsi page has Karamanlis sworn in at 4 a.m. on 24 July 1974 by Archbishop Seraphim and Gizikis staying 'temporarily in power for legal continuity reasons'. The land (all of Greece) is the reading of the state's name; the page gives no boundary.

certainty.note: Greece's land frontiers are treaty lines unchanged on the pages opened; the Aegean and Cyprus questions concern sea and other states' land, not Greek land, and were not opened.

sources.title: Metapolitefsi
sources.note: Karamanlis sworn in 4 a.m. 24 July 1974, the November 1974 election and the 1974 plebiscite on the monarchy.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Third Hellenic Republic' 1976..2024 (3 shapes: 122,017 / 121,731 / 121,731 km2). The Republic starts on 24 July 1974 (page), two years before the row, so one new keyframe covers 1974-75 and the junta's dossier ends in July 1974. The two pages opened give no Greek territorial event at all: no ledger event is written for 1992 (a 286 km2 shape difference, unverified) and no war is listed because the pages are silent on the Aegean disputes (Imia 1996, continental shelf), the Cyprus question for Greece after 1974 and western Thrace. Constitutional dates seen but with no territorial effect: the 1974 plebiscite (page: 'the 1974 plebiscite on the abolition of the monarchy', no day), Constitution of 11 June 1975, European Communities in 1981, Prespa Agreement (undated on the page). Rulers not written (the page lists only Gizikis July-December 1974 and Stasinopoulos 1974-75). Page budget 1-2 pages spent on 2.
